continuous random variable|continuous va: a variable that can take any value on an interval of the number line, such as a wait of 6.3 minutes; the probability of one exact value is 0, and a probability is an area. See [Probability is an area](#/math3042-q8/area-is-probability).
probability density function|pdf|density: $f(x)$, the height of the curve at $x$; the area under it between two values is the probability of landing between them, and the whole area is 1. See [Probability is an area](#/math3042-q8/area-is-probability).
cumulative distribution function|cdf: $F(x) = P(X \le x)$, the area under the curve to the left of $x$; $P(a \le X \le b) = F(b) - F(a)$. See [Probability is an area](#/math3042-q8/area-is-probability).
uniform distribution|uniform: every value between $a$ and $b$ is equally likely: a rectangle of height $1/(b-a)$, with $\mu = (a+b)/2$ and $\sigma = (b-a)/\sqrt{12}$. See [Uniform on paper](#/math3042-q8/uniform-on-paper).
normal distribution|bell curve|Gaussian: the bell-shaped curve, symmetric about its mean $\mu$, with width set by its standard deviation $\sigma$. See [The normal curve](#/math3042-q8/normal-curve).
standard normal|Z-distribution: the normal distribution with $\mu = 0$ and $\sigma = 1$, the one the Z table is printed for. See [The Z table](#/math3042-q8/z-table).
Z score|z-score|standardize: $Z = (x - \mu)/\sigma$, the number of standard deviations a value sits above (positive) or below (negative) the mean. See [Any normal on paper](#/math3042-q8/normal-on-paper).
Z table: the printed table that gives the area to the left of $z$, for $z$ to two decimals: the row is $z$ to one decimal and the column is the second decimal. See [The Z table](#/math3042-q8/z-table).
empirical rule: for a normal distribution, about 68 % of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, 95 % within two and 99.7 % within three. See [The normal curve](#/math3042-q8/normal-curve).
unusual: a value more than two standard deviations from the mean: $Z$ below $-2$ or above $2$. See [Any normal on paper](#/math3042-q8/normal-on-paper).
percentile: the value with a stated percentage of the area to its left; the 95th percentile has 0.95 to its left. See [From a percentage back to a value](#/math3042-q8/normal-backwards).
median: the 50th percentile: half the area lies on each side. For an exponential it is $\beta\ln 2$. See [Exponential backwards and memoryless](#/math3042-q8/exponential-percentile-memoryless).
exponential distribution|exponential: the distribution of the waiting time until the next event when events arrive at random at a steady average rate; $F(x) = 1 - e^{-x/\beta}$, $\mu = \beta$, $\sigma = \beta$. See [Exponential on paper](#/math3042-q8/exponential-on-paper).
beta|β: the mean waiting time of an exponential distribution, equal to 1 divided by the rate, in the same time unit as the question. See [Exponential on paper](#/math3042-q8/exponential-on-paper).
memoryless: the property of the exponential distribution that the time already waited has no influence on how much longer the wait will be. See [Exponential backwards and memoryless](#/math3042-q8/exponential-percentile-memoryless).
punif|pnorm|pexp: R's area-to-the-left functions: `punif(q, min, max)`, `pnorm(q, mean, sd)`, `pexp(q, rate)` with `rate` equal to $1/\beta$. See [punif, pnorm, pexp](#/math3042-q8/r-p-functions).
qunif|qnorm|qexp: R's percentile functions, the reverse of the p functions: give an area to the left, get the value back. See [qnorm, qexp, qunif](#/math3042-q8/r-q-functions).
runif|rnorm|rexp: R's random-value functions: `runif(n, min, max)`, `rnorm(n, mean, sd)`, `rexp(n, rate)` each make `n` simulated values. See [runif, rexp, rnorm](#/math3042-q8/r-simulate-continuous).
interquartile range|IQR: the third quartile minus the first, $Q_3 - Q_1$: the width of the middle half of the distribution. See [qnorm, qexp, qunif](#/math3042-q8/r-q-functions).
knit: RStudio's button that re-runs every chunk of the notebook from the top in a fresh session and writes the Word file Part 2 is marked on.
